title: Betrayed on Day 5: When China Fought the Caliphate | Talas 751
description:
In July 751 Tang China and the Abbasid Caliphate fought their only battle, by the Talas River on today's Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan border. For four days Tang crossbows held. On the fifth day the Karluk Turks switched sides, and the Tang army collapsed. But did Talas really decide Central Asia's future? Did it bring paper to the West? And what happened to the men who fought there? We check the sources.

Chapters
0:00 Two empires meet
Two worlds / The spark / How many men? / Five days / The collapse / The prisoner / Myth check / Did it change the map? / What happened to them

Who really won at Talas: the Abbasids, the Karluks, or the An Lushan rebellion four years later? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for the next battle.

Army sizes and losses are disputed: Chinese and Arab sources disagree a lot, and medieval numbers are often exaggerated. We show the ranges.
